setting: A fictional funding meeting where the learner and a teammate propose an idea to a decision-maker.

presentation.situation: You and your teammate {{mate}} want {{name}}, the director, to fund {{proposal}}, at {{cost}}. Your evidence: {{evidence}}. Limitation: {{limit}}. Recommend early, use evidence, and answer an objection.
presentation.opening: You have five minutes to convince me that {{proposal}} is worth funding. Go ahead.

brief.you_are: You are presenting a funding proposal with a teammate.
brief.situation: You and your teammate {{mate}} want {{name}}, the director, to fund {{proposal}}, at {{cost}}. Your evidence: {{evidence}}. Limitation: {{limit}}. Recommend early, use evidence, and answer an objection.
brief.task: State your recommendation early, use your evidence, and answer an objection. Your teammate can help if you bring them in.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} has a clear recommendation, your evidence, and a real answer to the main objection.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are presenting a funding proposal with a teammate.
goals: State your recommendation early, use your evidence, and answer an objection. Your teammate can help if you bring them in.

card.want: A proposal that is worth the money, and honesty about the risks.
card.hidden_need: Has been let down by an over-promised project before.
card.attitude: Sharp, fair and short of time.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Ask what happens if it fails

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

participants.name: {{mate}}
participants.relationship: On your side; helped to prepare the proposal

card.want: To support your case, without taking over.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Add a supporting fact only if asked or if things stall
Never speak for the whole team

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: {{name}} is worried about value for money.

objectives.evidence: The learner states the recommendation near the start.
alternatives: I recommend we fund a three-month trial.

objectives.evidence: The learner supports the case with the supplied evidence.
alternatives: The evidence shows that errors fell during the pilot.

objectives.evidence: The learner responds to an objection directly.
alternatives: I understand that concern; however, a limited trial reduces the risk.

opportunity: Bottom line: what are you asking for?
What do you want me to approve?
beats.orient: You have to convince me to fund this. Tell me first what you recommend.
fallback: What do you want me to approve?
Bottom line: what are you asking for?

opportunity: Why should I believe that will work?
beats.orient: Give me your evidence from the brief. You can also ask {{mate}} to add a detail.
fallback: Why should I believe that will work?
beats.second_line: I can add one detail from the pilot, if that helps.

opportunity: {{cost}} is a lot of money. Why should I spend it on this?
beats.orient: I have raised an objection about the cost. Answer it directly. Start with: I understand that concern.
fallback: {{cost}} is a lot of money. Why should I spend it on this?

closing_line: All right. You've made a fair case. I'll take that forward.

common_mistakes: Building up slowly to the point
o1.micro_lesson: Say: I recommend, in your first sentence.
o1.model: I recommend we fund a three-month trial.

o2.good: Using real evidence, and naming its limits.
common_mistakes: Claiming more than the evidence shows
o2.micro_lesson: Say: The evidence shows, and name a limit.
o2.model: The evidence shows errors fell, though it is only one team so far.

o3.good: Accepting the objection, and then answering it.
o3.micro_lesson: Say: I understand that concern; however.
o3.model: I understand that concern; however, a short trial limits the risk.

variants.name: Farah
variants.evidence: in a small pilot, average reply time fell from 9 hours to 5 hours
variants.limit: the pilot covered only one team

variants.name: James
variants.evidence: new staff in last year's trial reached full productivity two weeks earlier
variants.limit: the trial had only ten people
